test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: By selling an article at (3)/(8) of its actual selling price, Nirbhay incurs a loss of 13%. If he sells it at 70% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the actual selling price (SPₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ) be 8 units.

New SP = 3 units, which corresponds to a loss of 13% ⇒ 87% of CP.

Unitary method: 3 units ⇒ 87% ∴ 1 unit ⇒ 29%.

If he sells at 70% of 8 units = 5.6 units.

New SP in percentage = 5.6 × 29% = 162.4% of CP.

Profit% = 162.4% − 100% = 62.4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 62.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Case 1: SP₁ = 3/8 × SPₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ, Loss = 13%. Case 2: SP₂ = 0.70 × SPₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 ± P/L)% | Profit% = (SP/CP − 1) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be527b2ee96fda7d6c78652344550a07006e2f52038b748c2af806b4278da65b.png] 
⇒ Let SPₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ = S. Then 3/8 × S = CP × 0.87.
⇒ S = (CP × 0.87 × 8) ÷ 3 = CP × 0.29 × 8 = 2.32 × CP.
⇒ New selling price SP₂ = 70% of S = 0.70 × 2.32 × CP.
⇒ SP₂ = 1.624 × CP.
⇒ Profit% = (1.624 − 1) × 100 = 62.4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 62.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between SP and CP

When there is a **loss** of L%, SP = CP × (100 − L)/100. When there is a **profit** of P%, SP = CP × (100 + P)/100.

Unitary Method in Percentage

Comparing different selling prices to a fixed **Cost Price** (100%) allows for direct ratio calculations to find unknown profit or loss percentages.</p
